newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico labor leader suffered recent illness.
newsitem.headline: Mexico labor leader suffered recent illness.

text.p: Veteran Mexican labor leader Fidel Velasquez was seriously ill recently, causing him to go for 21 days without food or sleep, a colleague said on Wednesday.
Velasquez, 97, has been in and out of hospitals during the past few months for various ailments. He has been Mexico's undisputed labor king for five decades.
"The man is very tired," said Leonardo Rodriguez Alcaine, undersecretary at Velasquez's Mexican Workers Confederation (CTM), told Televisa television network in an interview.
"He went 21 days without eating or sleeping," he added, without describing Velasquez's current condition.
Velasquez, who has close ties to the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party, has cancelled his traditional Monday news conferences for two weeks running, fueling speculation about his health.
